subject: Trying to post a legend but not working

messages.author: 79e541c6b6654951
messages.subject: Trying to post a legend but not working
parts:
Hi All,
I am trying to create a bar graph using ggplot.

Here is my script:

std_plot=ggplot(data=orig_quant, aes(orig_quant$std_curve_rsq)) + 
  geom_histogram(breaks=seq(min(orig_quant$std_curve_rsq)-sd(orig_quant$std_curve_rsq), max(orig_quant$std_curve_rsq)+sd(orig_quant$std_curve_rsq), by = sd(orig_quant$std_curve_rsq)), 
                 col="red", 
                 fill="green", 
                 alpha = .2) + 
  labs(title="Quantitation Std_Curve_Rsq") +
  labs(x="std_curve_rsq", y="Frequency") + 
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=mean(orig_quant$std_curve_rsq,na.rm=T)),color="red", linetype="solid", size=2)+
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=flowcell_batch_value$std_curve_rsq,na.rm=T),color="blue", linetype="solid", size=2))

for reference, orig_quant is a set of data and std_curve_rsq is the column of data.
What I am also doing is drawing a line at the mean of the data set, and a line at where the users data is (flowcell_batch_value_std_curve).

What I want is to is have a legend that states the values of both those lines. The mean and the user value.
I tried doing that by using examples from here:
http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/Legends_%28ggplot2%29/

but it hasnt been working...do you know why it it hasnt been working?

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Trying to post a legend but not working
parts:
Start by eliminating $ inside aes(). You should never use $ inside aes
with ggplot2.

If you want more specific help, I'd recommend creating a minimal
reproducible example that others can easily copy and paste into R.

Hadley
